## Fixed decisions
- C-MODEL@1 in full. `modelForMemory` is renamed `recommendedModelForMemory`
  and no longer selects anything: it is the informational "this machine could
  also run X" recommendation, and `LARGE_TIER_GIB`/`DEFAULT_TIER_GIB` keep
  meaning what they mean.
- **Resolver shape.** `shared/src/effective-model.ts` exports
  `effectiveModel(input: { override?: string | null; installed: readonly string[] | null }): { tag: string; source: 'override' | 'promoted'; present: boolean | null }`.
  `override` is the `llm_model` setting (or the installer's `--model`), trimmed;
  blank or absent means no override. `installed` is the runtime's installed-tag
  list, or `null` when the runtime could not be asked — `null` and `[]` are
  different facts and must never be conflated. `present` is `true` when
  `installed` contains `tag`, `false` when `installed` is a list that does not,
  and `null` when `installed` is `null`: an unreachable runtime is **unknown**,
  never "not present", so a machine that did not answer is not reported as
  missing a model it has. `source` is `'override'` or `'promoted'` and nothing
  else, in the reachable and unreachable cases alike — `tag` and `source` come
  from the setting and a constant, not from the runtime, and the unreachable
  case is carried by `present: null` alone. The resolver is pure and never
  fetches: `server/src/ai/profiles.ts` exports the installed list
  (`readonly string[] | null`, built on today's 2s `/api/tags` cache, whose
  empty-set-on-error is what becomes `null`), and the server resolution and the
  health route both feed the resolver from it. The profile-availability list
  keeps today's behaviour for an unreadable runtime.
- **The installed list is injectable at the health route.** A stub
  `providers.llm` decides only what `describe()` says, so it cannot by itself
  make `present` `false`; the list does. `buildHealthResponse(config, db,
  providers, installedModels?: readonly string[] | null)` gains a fourth
  parameter and `BuildAppOptions` (`server/src/app.ts:31-49`) gains the
  matching field, so `server/src/routes/health.test.ts` passes
  `installedModels: ['some-other-tag']` for `present: false`,
  `installedModels: null` for `present: null` and
  `installedModels: ['qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M']` for `present: true` — with no
  listener and no stub HTTP server anywhere in the row. Production passes
  nothing, so the route asks `profiles.ts` exactly as it does today.
- **The health change is additive, and the three new keys are optional in the
  schema.** `HealthResponseSchema.ollama` gains
  `tag: string`, `source: 'override' | 'promoted'` and `present: boolean | null`
  **alongside** `reachable`, `model: string | null` and `modelPresent: boolean`,
  as `.extend({ tag: z.string().optional(), source: z.enum(['override', 'promoted']).optional(), present: z.boolean().nullable().optional() })`
  on the `ollama` object. Nothing is renamed or removed, and because
  `HealthResponse` is `z.infer` of it (`shared/src/health.ts:71`) an added key
  would otherwise become a **required** key and break the two typed literals in
  Must-not-edit `web/**` — `web/src/lib/setup.test.ts:11` and
  `web/src/test/fakeApi.ts:300`. Both stay exactly as they are, untouched, and
  still typecheck. The route always emits all three, so the response it sends
  is never the short shape; only the *type* admits it.
  `web/src/lib/setup.ts:81,129` and `web/src/components/AiBanner.tsx` keep
  compiling and behaving exactly as they do today. The three new fields are the
  resolver's answer; `model` and `modelPresent` keep their current
  `describe()`-derived values.
- **The agreement rule is real mode only, and fake mode reports the fake
  provider.** In fake mode there is no runtime to ask, so the route does not
  read the installed list: `tag` and `source` are still the resolver's answer
  for the stored `llm_model` (the promoted default and `'promoted'` when no
  override is set) and `present` is `true`, because
  `FakeLlmProvider.describe()` (`server/src/ai/fake.ts:262-269`) reports the
  model as present. `model` stays `'fake-llm'` and `modelPresent` stays `true`,
  so the setup screen keeps showing the fake model and
  `server/src/app.test.ts:31` keeps passing unedited. The rule below is
  asserted only when `!config.fakeAi`.
- **The agreement rule.** When `config.fakeAi` is false and `reachable` is
  true, `model` and `present` must agree — `model === tag` and
  `modelPresent === (present === true)` — and
  `server/src/routes/health.test.ts` asserts it; a disagreement is a bug in this
  card, not a tolerated difference. In real mode `present` is `null` exactly
  when `reachable` is false.
- **The promoted default is a new constant.** `shared/src/models.ts` adds
  `PROMOTED_DEFAULT_MODEL = 'qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M'`, and the resolver returns it
  whenever there is no override. `LARGE_MODEL`, `DEFAULT_MODEL` and `SMALL_MODEL`
  keep their current values and their current recommendation meanings, so
  `DEFAULT_MODEL` is still the *middle* tier and is **not** redefined to the
  promoted tag. The promoted tag's value is the current `SMALL_MODEL` value, so
  `installer/src/catalog.ts`'s `WRITING_MODELS` (keyed by tag string) already
  resolves it and needs no edit, and the tag literals in `scripts/setup-macos.sh`
  and `scripts/preflight-macos.sh` do not change.
- **`llm_profile` is not a second override path, and the "cloud" filter stays a
  guard.** `effectiveModel` reads `llm_model` only. `LLM_PROFILES.quick.model`
  stays as that profile's tag for `llm_available_profiles` and must equal the
  promoted default, asserted in `server/src/ai/profiles.test.ts`; the profile
  label the settings screen shows is unchanged, so no stored `llm_profile` value
  changes meaning. The resolver does not judge locality or weight format: a
  non-empty stored override is resolved as `source: 'override'`, and
  `isLocalModelTag` and `assertSupportedModelName` remain the guards at the use
  site, unchanged. An override a guard rejects is reported `present: false`,
  because a cloud name is never in the local installed list — health says "your
  setting is in effect and that model is not here", which is the truth, rather
  than silently resolving and showing a different tag. The `isLocalModelTag`
  gate **leaves** `configuredModel` (`server/src/ai/profiles.ts:72`): it no
  longer falls back to the profile tag for a cloud override, because the
  resolver decides and `source` is `'override'` for any non-empty stored value.
  The existing row "never selects cloud-backed configured models"
  (`server/src/ai/profiles.test.ts:45-52`) is **updated to the new policy, not
  deleted** — the same treatment `installer/src/run.test.ts` gets below.
- **Machine reading survives only for the recommendation.**
  `defaultModelForMachine()` stops selecting: `server/src/ai/ollama.ts:231` falls
  back to the promoted default and `server/src/eval/cli.ts` defaults to the
  promoted default. The name stays exported from
  `server/src/ai/model-picker.ts`, returning the promoted default, because
  `scripts/smoke-live.mjs:39,217` imports it dynamically and that script is
  outside this card's scope; it is a historical name, not a second policy.
  `machineMemoryGib()` survives only as the input to
  `recommendedModelForMemory()`. `installer/src/cli.ts` and
  `installer/src/machine.ts` need no change — `PlanInput.memoryGib` and
  `PlanEvent.memoryGib` stay and are informational.
- **Exports.** `shared/src/index.ts` exports `effectiveModel` and its input and
  result types, and `recommendedModelForMemory`, in the block that re-exports
  `./models.js` today (which loses the `modelForMemory` line), so
  `@apunta/shared`'s single `exports` entry carries the new module deliberately
  rather than by accident. `shared/package.json` is not touched.
- **The setup UI does not move in this card.** `web/**` keeps reading
  `ollama.model` and `ollama.modelPresent`; that is exactly why the health
  change is additive. Collapsing the two pairs into one is deferred, and the
  follow-up is recorded in the return file rather than done here.
- **The installer's `reason`.** `ChosenModel.reason` may no longer cite the
  machine's memory as the reason. For a promoted tag it says Apunta uses the
  same writing model on every machine and that this one was not chosen from
  this Mac's memory; for an override it keeps naming the tag and says it was
  chosen for the machine rather than by Apunta. `PlanEvent.memoryGib` is still
  reported. The recommendation is not added to a new surface in this card;
  `scripts/preflight-macos.sh` may print it as one informational line.
- **The eval digest is not this card's.** C-MODEL@1's "every measurement records
  tag and digest" is S3.2's obligation (`docs/v2/cards/S3.2.md`, Fixed
  decisions: the report records the model tag and digest), and nothing in
  `server/src/eval/` records a digest at the base commit. P1.4 proves the eval
  *default tag* and nothing about digests; adding `ollama show` here would be a
  new measurement path, not a resolver change.
- **Test isolation (HS-2):** V1/V2 run the repository's own vitest suite, which
  opens only temporary databases created by `server/src/test/harness.ts` and by
  `mkdtempSync` under the OS temp dir
  (`server/src/routes/health.test.ts:31-33`), never the platform data folder and
  never the live instance. No test in these rows calls `listen` —
  `health.test.ts` drives `buildApp` and `server.inject` (`:50,61,72`) — and no
  sandbox port is bound, so as in RUN-CONFIG §3 these rows run bare and port

# Contract excerpts (authoritative)

## C-MODEL@1 Effective writing model

**Built by** P1.4. **Proven by** P1.4, P4.3, Q1.1. **Consumers:** installer
plan, setup screens, server generation and preload, health and preflight,
eval CLI, check scripts.

One resolver in `shared/` (browser-safe, no installer import):
`effectiveModel({ override, installed }): { tag, source }`.

| Case | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `llm_model` setting is a non-empty tag | that tag, `source: 'override'` |
| no override | `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`, `source: 'promoted'` |

- Memory size never selects the model. `modelForMemory()` may remain as an
  **informational recommendation** in setup ("this machine could also run
  X"), never as a selection, and is renamed to say so.
- Setup downloads exactly the effective model. A clean install makes its
  first inference without any further pull.
- Health and preflight report `{ tag, source, present }`.
- The eval CLI with no `--models` uses the promoted default, not the memory
  picker. Every measurement records tag **and digest** (`ollama show`).

**Normal example.** 16 GiB machine, no override → setup downloads
`qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M`; the server uses it; eval default uses it.

**Rejection example.** Override set to a tag that is not installed → health
reports `present: false` and generation returns the existing "model not
available" error; nothing is pulled automatically.

# Run configuration (v2 plan)

## 1. Ports

| Use | Port |
| --- | --- |
| Live instance: **never contact** | 7717 |
| Sandbox servers (C-ISO) | 7800 to 7889 |
| Updater test server (C-UPD) | 7890 to 7899 |
| Playwright under the sandbox | the port `sandbox.mjs env` assigns |

## 2. Gate levels

A card names one level. Commands run from the repository root unless a card
says otherwise. Until P0.3 is APPROVED, only L0 and the non-launching part of
L1 may run.

| Level | When | Commands |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **L0** docs only | cards that change only Markdown | `npx prettier --check <changed files>`; `node scripts/check-no-external-urls.mjs` |
| **L1** targeted | every implementation card | `npm run lint`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run build:shared`, then the card's named test files with `npx vitest run <paths>` from the repository root (the root `vitest.config.ts` defines the projects) |
| **L2** parent acceptance | every parent review card | everything in §3 |
| **L3** native or real model | cards and parent reviews that say so | the card's listed commands, all through `sandbox.mjs` |

## 3. The L2 suite

```sh
npm run lint
npm run typecheck
TZ=UTC npm test
TZ=America/Denver npm test
TZ=America/Mexico_City npm test
TZ=Australia/Sydney npm test
npm run build
node scripts/v2/sandbox.mjs env --port 7810 > /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && . /tmp/apunta-v2-e2e.env && npm run e2e
npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1
```

After P0.2, each `TZ=` run prints its effective zone (a test asserts it), so
four runs really exercise four zones. After P0.3, the e2e line is the only
permitted way to run Playwright. After S3.2, add
`npm run eval -- --fake --runs 1 --corpus e2e/fixtures/eval-es/tuning`.
After P3.3, add `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` and
`cargo test` in `src-tauri/`.

## 4. Evidence

- Write detailed output to `docs/v2/evidence/<card-id>/`. Keep it sanitized:
  replace sandbox paths with `<sandbox>`, the home folder with `~`, and never
  include hostnames, usernames, keys, tokens or real names.
- Raw logs stay in the sandbox run folder and are never committed.
- Each command's evidence records: working directory, exact command, exit
  code, start and end time, and a short excerpt (failures in full, up to 200
  lines).
- Status words: criteria `NOT RUN`, `PASS`, `FAIL`, `BLOCKED`; cards
  `NOT STARTED`, `IN PROGRESS`, `SUBMITTED`, `APPROVED`,
  `CHANGES REQUESTED`, `BLOCKED`; instruction reviews `CLEAR`, `DEFECT`,
  `UNKNOWN`. Every blank template starts at `NOT RUN` or `UNKNOWN`.

## Numbered findings for the implementer

1. **The agreement rule is not implemented, and the test that is supposed to
   assert it cannot fail.** `server/src/routes/health.ts:53-69` computes `present`
   from the installed list alone and never consults `llm.reachable` (which is
   read at `:42` and only used at `:84`). The card's fixed decision 5 says, in
   full: "In real mode `present` is `null` exactly when `reachable` is false",
   and two sentences earlier, "a disagreement is a bug in this card, not a
   tolerated difference". The route can emit both forbidden states through the
   card's own documented seam — `installedModels: null` with a reachable
   `describe()`, and a reachable-false `describe()` with a list that answered.
   My probe (step 3, supplementary 2) produced exactly those two:
   `reachable: true, modelPresent: true, present: null` and
   `reachable: false, present: true`. In production the two probes are
   independent round trips to the same loopback URL — `OllamaProvider.describe()`
   fetches `/api/tags` at `ollama.ts:246` and `readInstalledModelNames` fetches it
   again at `profiles.ts:68`, each with its own 2500 ms timeout, and the second
   may be answered from the 2 s cache while the first was not — so the states are
   transient rather than hypothetical, and P4.3 and Q1.1 are named as consumers
   of `{ tag, source, present }`.
   The test half is the sharper half: `server/src/routes/health.test.ts:253`
   derives `modelPresent` from `installedModels.includes(PROMOTED_DEFAULT_MODEL)`
   — the same array it injects at `:255` — so the assertion at `:261` is a
   tautology that holds for every input the loop can produce, and the loop never
   decorrelates `reachable` from `present`. The row at `:272` is named "reports
   present: null exactly when the runtime is unreachable" but tests only the one
   consistent direction.
   *What would make it pass:* in `buildHealthResponse`, derive the installed
   argument as `llm.reachable ? (injectedInstalledModels === undefined ? await
   installedModelTags({ baseUrl: config.ollamaUrl }) : injectedInstalledModels) :
   null`, so `present === null` iff `!reachable` holds by construction; and add
   the two decorrelated rows (`reachable: true` + `installedModels: null`;
   `reachable: false` + `installedModels: [PROMOTED_DEFAULT_MODEL]`) so the
   agreement row asserts the route rather than the test's own construction. Note
   for the coordinator, not for you: with `model`/`modelPresent` fixed by the
   card to stay `describe()`-derived and the three new fields fixed to be the
   resolver's answer over an injected list, *full* agreement cannot be guaranteed
   by construction for the remaining "reachable, list read failed" state. If the
   card's wording is meant literally, it needs relaxing to the steady state, and
   that is the coordinator's sentence to change — say so in the return file rather
   than widening the change.

2. **`configuredModel` re-implements the resolver instead of calling it, and the
   server's own resolution is dead code in production.**
   `server/src/ai/profiles.ts:145-147` is
   `llmModelOverride(db) ?? LLM_PROFILES.quick?.model ?? PROMOTED_DEFAULT_MODEL`
   — the resolver's selection rule written a second time, by hand. Meanwhile
   `resolveEffectiveModel` (`:132-143`), which is the function the card's
   decision 2 describes as "the server resolution", has **no production caller**:
   `grep` finds it only in `profiles.test.ts`. The generation path runs
   `ai/index.ts:37` → `resolveModel` → `resolveLlmProfile` → `configuredModel`, so
   the resolver is called in production from exactly two places (the installer
   plan and the health route) and the eval CLI uses the constant directly.
   Behaviour is identical today and `profiles.test.ts:65-67` would catch a drift
   in `LLM_PROFILES.quick.model`, so nothing is wrong for the owner; but
   C-MODEL@1's "one resolver" is currently enforced by a test rather than by the
   code, and the three functions that decide a tag are the three a future edit
   has to keep in step. *What would make it pass:* express `configuredModel` as
   `effectiveModel({ override: llmModelOverride(db), installed: null }).tag` (the
   `LLM_PROFILES.quick?.model` term is redundant once the equality is pinned),
   and either wire `resolveEffectiveModel` into the generation path or say in the
   return file why the server resolves the tag without the `present` half.

3. **`scripts/setup-macos.sh` and `scripts/preflight-macos.sh` still decide the
   model from RAM — residual, and the card's May-edit wording is why.**
   `scripts/setup-macos.sh:311-323` picks `MODEL` from `RAM_GIB` and
   `scripts/setup-macos.sh:352` runs `ollama pull "$MODEL"`, so a 16 or 32 GiB Mac
   still downloads `gemma4:12b-it-qat` while the app, health and eval all resolve
   `qwen3.5:4b-q4_K_M` — the exact R03 drift ("16 GiB: setup picks gemma4, app
   uses qwen") that this card exists to close, and a direct miss on C-MODEL@1's
   "Setup downloads exactly the effective model. A clean install makes its first
   inference without any further pull" on that path.
   `scripts/preflight-macos.sh:315` is worse than stale, because it is stated as
   fact to the owner: "memory unreadable, so Apunta would pick the fallback
   model: $SMALL_TAG", and `:327` "tier: $TIER_NAME → $TIER_TAG".
   You did nothing wrong here and you should not fix it unilaterally: the card
   permits `preflight-macos.sh` edits only as "one informational line" of
   recommendation, and permits `setup-macos.sh` edits "only if a tag literal has
   to change — it should not". Both readings forbid changing a *selection*.
   *What would make it pass:* escalate it. The owner-facing path is the packaged
   app's first-run window (`docs/INSTALL.md` §1 is a DMG), so this is not a
   first-run blocker, but a developer or a second Mac provisioned by
   `setup-macos.sh` will hit it. P4.3 may edit both scripts but only for "model
   list text", so no card currently owns the selection. The coordinator should
